quests.sentenceWithBlank: The negotiations had every reason to fail, ____ somehow both sides walked away satisfied.
quests.completedSentence: The negotiations had every reason to fail, yet somehow both sides walked away satisfied.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' introduces this contrast in a reflective register, much like 'but' would. 'So' would incorrectly suggest the doomed odds caused the successful outcome.
quests.nativeTip: Both sides walking away satisfied despite every reason to fail is the surprising twist here - a reflective, slightly formal tone.
quests.example: The negotiations had every reason to fail, yet somehow both sides walked away satisfied.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The store doesn't carry that brand anymore, ____ does it plan to restock similar items.
quests.completedSentence: The store doesn't carry that brand anymore, nor does it plan to restock similar items.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' continues the negative statement with the required inversion - 'does it plan.' 'And' would need normal word order and wouldn't match this sentence as written.
quests.nativeTip: Watch the inverted verb order after the blank - it signals which connector continues this negative statement.
quests.example: The store doesn't carry that brand anymore, nor does it plan to restock similar items.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The forecast promised a clear evening, ____ the fireworks were canceled anyway due to a sudden fog.
quests.completedSentence: The forecast promised a clear evening, but the fireworks were canceled anyway due to a sudden fog.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' captures this everyday contradiction between the forecast and the cancellation. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the clear forecast the cause of the cancellation.
quests.nativeTip: The cancellation despite a clear forecast is an everyday, straightforward contrast, not a formal comparison.
quests.example: The forecast promised a clear evening, but the fireworks were canceled anyway due to a sudden fog.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The choir postponed its spring concert ____ half the soloists had come down with the same flu.
quests.completedSentence: The choir postponed its spring concert because half the soloists had come down with the same flu.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason - the illness among soloists. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the postponement the cause of the flu.
quests.nativeTip: This explains the actual reason for the postponement, not an outcome or a goal.
quests.example: The choir postponed its spring concert because half the soloists had come down with the same flu.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Half the soloists came down with the same flu, ____ the choir had no choice but to postpone its spring concert.
quests.completedSentence: Half the soloists came down with the same flu, so the choir had no choice but to postpone its spring concert.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' shows the flu directly led to the postponement. 'Because' would only fit if the reason came after the outcome, which isn't the order here.
quests.nativeTip: This time the cause comes first, and the outcome follows.
quests.example: Half the soloists came down with the same flu, so the choir had no choice but to postpone its spring concert.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The choir director scheduled two backup rehearsal dates ____ a single round of illness wouldn't derail the whole season.
quests.completedSentence: The choir director scheduled two backup rehearsal dates so that a single round of illness wouldn't derail the whole season.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'wouldn't' expressing the intended prevention. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a forward-looking goal.
quests.nativeTip: Scheduling backup dates was a deliberate step taken with a specific goal - protecting the season from future illness.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The choir director scheduled two backup rehearsal dates so that a single round of illness wouldn't derail the whole season.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The kids practiced their instruments ____ their mother prepared dinner in the next room.
quests.completedSentence: The kids practiced their instruments while their mother prepared dinner in the next room.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'While' shows two ongoing actions happening simultaneously. 'Before' or 'after' would suggest one finished before the other began, which isn't the picture here.
quests.nativeTip: Both activities - practicing and cooking - are happening at the same time here, in different rooms.
quests.example: The kids practiced their instruments while their mother prepared dinner in the next room.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The volunteers kept sorting donations ____ every last box had been checked and labeled.
quests.completedSentence: The volunteers kept sorting donations until every last box had been checked and labeled.
quests.grammarRule: Time - until (continuation up to a point)
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Until' captures this continuous sorting that stops exactly when everything is checked. 'Before' would only mark a single point, missing the sense of ongoing work.
quests.nativeTip: The sorting continued without stopping, right up to the moment every box was done - this is about ongoing duration.
quests.example: The volunteers kept sorting donations until every last box had been checked and labeled.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the last guest had signed the register, the wedding planner finally allowed herself to relax.
quests.completedSentence: once the last guest had signed the register, the wedding planner finally allowed herself to relax.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Once' emphasizes that the final signature directly triggered her relief. 'When' could describe simple timing but doesn't capture this completion-triggers-relief relationship as precisely.
quests.nativeTip: The last guest signing in is the specific trigger for her relief, not just a general point in time.
quests.example: once the last guest had signed the register, the wedding planner finally allowed herself to relax.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the recipe had never failed the baker before, the cake collapsed completely this time.
quests.completedSentence: although the recipe had never failed the baker before, the cake collapsed completely this time.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the reliable recipe and the surprising failure. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of surprising twist.
quests.nativeTip: The cake collapsing despite a flawless track record is the unexpected twist here.
quests.example: although the recipe had never failed the baker before, the cake collapsed completely this time.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The east trail winds gently through the forest, ____ the west trail climbs sharply toward the ridge.
quests.completedSentence: The east trail winds gently through the forest, whereas the west trail climbs sharply toward the ridge.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting trail descriptions. 'Although' would suggest the west trail climbs sharply despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship here.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the team had lost their star player to injury in the first quarter, they still pulled off the upset.
quests.completedSentence: even though the team had lost their star player to injury in the first quarter, they still pulled off the upset.

quests.nativeTip: Losing the star player in the first quarter is a serious setback - this deserves the stronger of the two near-identical concession connectors.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ even though ]── Clause B
quests.example: even though the team had lost their star player to injury in the first quarter, they still pulled off the upset.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the museum extends its hours for the summer exhibit, we should plan a weekend trip to see it.

quests.ruleExplanation: 'If' introduces this uncertain possibility about the museum's hours. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a condition.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the highway bridge has been closed for repairs since March, commuters have had to find alternate routes every morning.
quests.completedSentence: since the highway bridge has been closed for repairs since March, commuters have had to find alternate routes every morning.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ ticket prices for the exhibit had tripled since its opening, the lines outside the museum were longer than ever.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The warranty will be voided ____ the device is registered within thirty days of purchase.
quests.completedSentence: The warranty will be voided unless the device is registered within thirty days of purchase.

quests.nativeTip: The warranty is voided specifically when registration does NOT happen in time - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.example: The warranty will be voided unless the device is registered within thirty days of purchase.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The climbers plan to reach the summit ____ the weather takes a turn overnight.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: You're free to borrow any of the tools in the shed ____ you put them back exactly where you found them.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: My phone battery was down to two percent before the flight ____ it somehow lasted the entire way.

quests.nativeTip: This is a relaxed, spoken-style observation - the more casual of the near-identical concession connectors fits here.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The grant will be renewed for a second year ____ the organization submits a full financial report by the deadline.

quests.nativeTip: This is formal grant language - the most formal of the condition phrases fits this official tone.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ provided that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The grant will be renewed for a second year provided that the organization submits a full financial report by the deadline.
